explanation: Build prerequisite-to-course edges and indegrees. Repeatedly remove a zero-indegree course and release its dependents. All courses are removable exactly when no directed cycle remains.
timeComplexity: O(V + E) time for V courses and E prerequisite pairs. Building adjacency and indegrees reads every edge; each vertex is removed once and each outgoing edge decremented once.
spaceComplexity: O(V + E) auxiliary space. Adjacency stores E edges, while indegrees and the ready queue each hold at most V entries.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Java algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Indegree counts the unprocessed prerequisites of each course. A zero-indegree course can be completed, and removing it decrements exactly its dependents’ remaining prerequisite counts. A directed acyclic graph eventually releases every vertex. If processing stops early, every remaining course depends within the remainder, proving a cycle.
walkthrough: For four courses with prerequisites [1,0],[2,1],[3,1], begin with course 0. Finishing it releases course 1; finishing 1 releases both 2 and 3. All four courses are processed, so return true.
edgeCases: Isolated courses also need to be included in the processed count.
No prerequisites makes every course immediately available.
